newsitem.title: USA: Arizona man convicted of killing his children.
newsitem.headline: Arizona man convicted of killing his children.

text.p: An Arizona man was convicted on Thursday of murdering his four daughters, gunning them down as they watched television because he was distraught over the breakup of his marriage, authorities said.
Norman Yazzie, 33, was charged with shooting his five children on Sept. 1 with a .22-calibre rifle in their trailer home in Dennehotso, a small, isolated community near the Arizona-Utah border.

The four girls -- Jazana, 13, Veneshia, 11, Cara, 8 and Nathalie, 5 -- were killed. Yazzie's 11-year-old son, Rhyan, survived and testified at the trial. Yazzie was convicted of attempted murder in the shooting of his son.
After the shootings, Yazzie fled the scene and left a note with the words: "Who has the last laugh here ... How does it feel now?"
He later told investigators "I just couldn't handle the idea of not being a family."

The identity and whereabouts of the children's mother did not come up at the trial, held at a federal court meeting in Prescott, about 100 miles north of Phoenix. The jury deliberated less than two hours before reaching the verdict.
Dennehotso is located within the Navajo Nation. The federal government has jurisdiction over crimes committed on Indian reservations.

Yazzie is scheduled to be sentenced in February and faces life in prison. Because the Navajo Nation does not recognise the death penalty, the prosecutors will not seek it nor would the judge impose it, authorities said. Yazzie is a member of the Navajo Nation.
The U.S. Attorney for Arizona, Janet Napolitano, said "This was a horrific crime. We hope that the community of Dennehotso can begin healing now after what happened to them."
